discovery: Prediction and experimental discovery of the quantum anomalous Hall effect in magnetic topological insulators

nominees.name: Qi-Kun Xue
nominees.affiliation: Southern University of Science and Technology and Tsinghua University, China

nominees.name: Zhong Fang
nominees.affiliation: Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, China

nominees.name: Xi Dai
nominees.affiliation: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Hong Kong, China

motivation: The quantum anomalous Hall effect is a quantized Hall resistance h/e^2 at zero magnetic field, carried by dissipationless chiral edge states. It was proposed by Haldane in 1988 but had never been realized. In 2010 Fang and Dai, with collaborators, showed from first principles that magnetically doped Bi2Se3-family topological insulators could host the effect and named realistic materials. Xue then led a long molecular-beam-epitaxy effort that controlled film thickness, magnetic doping and the Fermi level at the atomic scale. In 2013 his team observed the quantized plateau in Cr-doped (Bi,Sb)2Te3 (Science 340, 167). The result has since been reproduced and refined worldwide, reaching metrological precision. It is the first topological quantum state that needs no Landau levels, and it opened the fields of axion insulators, intrinsic magnetic topological materials such as MnBi2Te4, and zero-field quantum resistance standards. It is a model of theory predicting a result and patient materials work then realizing it.
